heading: Evaluate the engagement behind a tax-adviser review
body:
A review can help you identify questions, but it cannot establish whether a firm’s engagement fits your situation. Look for the work actually described: planning, return preparation, bookkeeping, payroll coordination, implementation, or ongoing advice. A favorable comment about one service does not confirm that another service is included.

Before comparing firms, write a short scope request using the same facts for each. State the entities, owners, states, property holdings, bookkeeping condition, and decisions you need help making. Ask which deliverables are included, what you must supply, who implements recommendations, and how additional work is priced. A fee comparison is meaningful only when the scopes are comparable.

When reading a testimonial, distinguish the client’s reported experience from independently verified outcomes. A selected example is not a forecast of your savings, and a published rating can change. Follow original review-platform links and note the date you checked them.

This site is an AE Tax Advisors resource. Use its disclosures and service information alongside independent research and the proposed engagement agreement. The decision should rest on supported credentials, relevant experience, clear responsibilities, and a scope you understand.
